svg.title: Debtor Examination and Follow-Up Levy Cost Stack
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-debtor-exam-cost-stack; chapter number: 4; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Debtor Examination and Follow-Up Levy Cost Stack; subtitle: California filing and levy costs reported by practitioners; total range: $60 exam order with a free writ, then $30 to $1,500 or more in levy deposits, plus $300 per 8 hours if a keeper is used; caption: The examination itself is cheap; the spend lands on the levies that must be ready to fire right after the exam, before the debtor moves money to a different bank.; assumptions note: Exam order and writ costs are Sacramento figures; levy deposit and keeper figures are California writ-of-execution costs from a separate source. The levy deposit high end is stated as $1,500 or more.; note: Sources - Sacramento County Public Law Library (HrhPbWDRBVU), Lawyer Tips by The Sterling Firm (UV-WyQ1-NC4).; buckets: label: Examination Order Filing; low: 60; high: 60; notes: Sacramento fee, with a court backlog of up to a month or more and a 150-mile reach; label: Writ of Execution Issued With the Order; low: 0; high: 0; notes: Issued at the same time for free in Sacramento; label: Levy Deposits; low: 30; high: 1500; notes: From bank and wage levies up to business and sale notices, $1,500 or more at the top; label: Keeper Per 8 Hours; low: 300; high: 300; notes: Keeper cost quoted per 8-hour block
